Rushmoor's population increased by around 5,900 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 100,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Rushmoor increased by 6.3%, from around 93,800 in 2011 to around 99,800 in 2021.

The population here increased by a smaller percentage than the overall population of the South East (7.5%), and by a smaller percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Rushmoor was home to around 18.2 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 17.2 in 2011. This area was among the top 25% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was lower in Rushmoor than across the South East

Median age increased

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Rushmoor increased by two years, from 36 to 38 years of age.

This area had a lower average (median) age than the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) and a lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 3,700 (an increase of 25.1%), while the number of residents between 35 and 49 years fell by around 1,100 (5.1% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 2.8 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Rushmoor residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 73,300 Rushmoor residents said they were born in England. This represented 73.5% of the local population. The figure has decreased from around 73,900 in 2011, which at the time represented 78.8% of Rushmoor's population.

Southern Asian countries (other than Afghanistan, India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka) were the next most represented, with around 8,400 Rushmoor residents reporting one of these countries as their country of birth (8.4%). This figure was up from just over 4,800 in 2011, which at the time represented 5.2% of the population of Rushmoor.

The number of Rushmoor residents born in India rose from just over 850 in 2011 (0.9% of the local population) to around 1,400 in 2021 (1.4%).

In 2021, 73.5% of Rushmoor residents reported their country of birth as England

More couples with non-dependent children

Rushmoor saw England's joint largest percentage-point rise (alongside Kensington and Chelsea and Redbridge) in the proportion of households including a couple with only non-dependent children (from 6.2% in 2011 to 7.4% in 2021).

Slough (from 6.0% to 7.1%) and Three Rivers (from 7.4% to 8.4%) saw the country's next largest increases in the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children.

The percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children in Rushmoor increased by 1.2 percentage points

National identity in Rushmoor

In 2021, 13.7% of Rushmoor residents did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK. This figure increased from 11.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just under 1 in 40 people (2.3%) identified with a UK and non-UK national identity, compared with 0.9% in 2011. The percentage of residents in Rushmoor that identified as "British only" increased from 16.9% to 52.9%.

The increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK was greater in Rushmoor (2.6 percentage points) than across the South East (1.6 percentage points, from 7.1% to 8.7%). Across England, the percentage increased by 1.7 percentage points, from 8.2% to 10.0%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Rushmoor increased by 2.6 percentage points

Rise in private renting

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Rushmoor (3.9 percentage points) than in nearby Hart (1.5 percentage points).

In Rushmoor, the percentage of private renting increased from 17.6% in 2011 to 21.5% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Hart increased from 12.1% to 13.6%.

The rate of social renting in Rushmoor fell from 16.3% to 16.2%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 63.5% to 60.5%.

Private renting in Rushmoor increased by 3.9 percentage points

Unpaid care in Rushmoor

In 2021, 3.8% of Rushmoor residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 6.4% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.5% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.2% in 2011. The proportion of Rushmoor residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.1% to 2.2%.

This area had the region’s third lowest proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care. Across the region, only Slough (3.3%) and Reading (3.7%) had a lower proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Rushmoor decreased by 2.6 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Rushmoor

In 2021, 14.7% of Rushmoor residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 10.4% in 2011. The 4.3 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 77.4% of people in Rushmoor identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 84.8% in 2011), while 2.8% identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") (compared with 0.6% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category increased from 2.2% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

Read the bulletin Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 14.7% of usual residents in Rushmoor identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

Religion in Rushmoor

In 2021, 37.9% of Rushmoor residents reported having "No religion", up from 26.4% in 2011. The rise of 11.5 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Rushmoor. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 42.3% of people in Rushmoor described themselves as Christian (down from 57.8%), while 5.7% described themselves as Hindu (up from 3.4% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 37.9% of usual residents in Rushmoor reported having "No religion"

Marriage and civil partnership in Rushmoor

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were married (or in a civil partnership) was greater in nearby Hart (3.7 percentage points) than in Rushmoor (1.6 percentage points).

In Rushmoor, the percentage of adults who were married or in a civil partnership decreased from 49.7% in 2011 to 48.1% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Hart decreased from 58.4% to 54.7%.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Rushmoor increased from 33.0% to 35.5%, while the percentage of adults who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership remained at 9.1%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who were married or in a civil partnership in Rushmoor decreased by 1.6 percentage points

Health in Rushmoor

In 2021, 47.1% of Rushmoor residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 45.4% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 36.6% to 35.5%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Rushmoor residents describing their health as "very bad" decreased from 1.1% to 0.9%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.6% to 3.4%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very bad health in Rushmoor decreased by 0.2 percentage points

Change in employment

Of Rushmoor residents aged 16 years and over, 64.2% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, down from 66.1% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 1 in 40 people (2.7%) said they were unemployed, compared with 3.5% in 2011. The percentage of retired Rushmoor residents increased from 15.5% to 17.2%.

This area had the region’s second highest percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed. Across the region, only Bracknell Forest, with 65.2%, had a higher percentage.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Rushmoor decreased by 2.0 percentage points

Fewer adults working long hours

In 2021, 10.6% of Rushmoor residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked over 49 hours per week. This figure decreased from 13.7% in 2011.

The decrease in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked over 49 hours per week was greater in Rushmoor (3.1 percentage points) than across the South East (2.7 percentage points, from 14.6% to 11.9%). Across England, the percentage fell by 2.2 percentage points, from 13.3% to 11.1%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults in employment who worked 49 hours or more in Rushmoor decreased by 3.1 percentage points

Disability in Rushmoor

In 2021, 6.0% of Rushmoor residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 7.3% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion who were identified as being disabled and limited a little remained at 9.6%, while the proportion of Rushmoor residents who were not disabled increased from 83.1% to 84.4%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot was greater in Rushmoor (1.3 percentage points) than across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Rushmoor decreased by 1.3 percentage points
